extent_reading: Durrett pp. 113-115: all of Section 3.1 (the chapter claims to supply it). Feller pp. 51-54: all of II.9 with its continuation, and (8.11) as the tool II.9 uses. Feller VI.3 pp. 150-151: the tail estimates (3.4)-(3.6) the text attaches the locator to. Feller VII.1 pp. 175, 179: Lemma 2 and its proof. Feller VII.2 pp. 179-181: the constant determination (footnote 3) and the steps (2.2)-(2.10) it amends.

components.note: Every convention is stated. Durrett p. 113 fair-sign walk and his ~ convention, Feller p. 52 / VII.1 fn 2 ~ convention. The 'previously proved Gaussian integral' is thm:p15-normal-normalization, earlier on the route.

Durrett Lemma 3.1.1 (statement and proof idea) and Exercise 3.1.1 (p. 114-115) are stated with written proofs. The expansion Feller II.9 takes from (8.11) (p. 51) is proved for the range II.9 uses (0<y<1), and the series remainder is bounded.

Feller VI.3 (3.4)-(3.6) (p. 151) are stated with the r>Np / r<Np hypotheses. The proof follows the ratio (3.1), the geometric comparison, the term count (with the ceiling of Np in place of the central index m) and the failure count. Feller VII.1 Lemma 2 (1.7)-(1.8) (p. 175) is proved by the derivative comparison (1.9) (p. 179).

components.gap: Feller II.9 is selected in full by the chapter's Stirling referral (Feller I, 3rd ed., pp. 52-54), and two of its justificatory claims are recorded nowhere on the route. (1) Feller pp. 52-53 motivates the key construction: the double inequality (9.5) suggests comparing log n! with a quantity close to the arithmetic mean of its two extreme members, the simplest such quantity being (n+1/2) log n - n, which is why d_n is defined as in (9.6). The annex (de-moivre-laplace-and-stirling.tex lines 123-126) only defines d_n 'as in Feller', without this reason. (2) Feller p. 53 says that the proof that e^C equals sqrt(2 pi) is elementary, does not depend on the material of his chapters IV-VI, and is put off to chapter VII only because it is naturally tied to the normal approximation theorem. Neither the body (lines 115-119), the annex constant argument (lines 171-253) nor the companion record (distributions-transforms-and-moment-problems-w02c-p15-011.tex lines 124-147, which reports only that Feller determines the constant in VII.2) states this claim. Nor do they reconcile it with the VII.2 argument followed here, which uses the chapter VI tail estimate VI,(3.5) (thm:p15-stirling-tail-premises, annex lines 222-234). Record both claims, and state how the independence claim relates to that use of VI,(3.5).
components.note: The mathematics is complete. Feller (9.2)-(9.15) are proved, including the (12n+1)(12n+13)-36(2n+1)^2 check. Footnote 17 is strengthened to an n^-5 bound (checked by machine). The VII.2 footnote 3 constant argument (pp. 180-181) runs with an unknown A: the central ratio, the Riemann sums, the VI,(3.5) tail and the (1.8) Gaussian bound. The cosine-integral second determination cites a lemma proved earlier on the route. Footnotes 14-16 are recorded in the companion chapter. Two II.9 justificatory claims are missing (see gap).

Durrett (3.1.2), the separation of the two leading factors, the three Lemma 3.1.1 limits, the k/n->0 step and Theorem 3.1.2 (pp. 113-114) are all present, with an exact Stirling remainder. The uniform bound K_A/n is derived and checked numerically. The odd parity comes from the two-term formula, and the extreme and wrong-parity points are handled.

Durrett Theorem 3.1.3 (p. 115) is present with the even Riemann-sum step (p. 114) and the S_{2n+1}=S_{2n}+-1 remark, plus exact indices, strict and singleton endpoints, the CDF limit and infinite endpoints. Durrett's remarks that this is a special case of the Section 3.4 CLT and that the computations are elementary (pp. 113, 115), and the chi = standard normal reading, are recorded in the companion chapter.
Durrett's i.i.d. Poisson(1) setting for Exercises 3.1.2 and 3.1.4 (p. 115) is stated, with T_n separate from S_N and the lambda=0 convention.
Durrett's claim that S_n is Poisson(n), P(S_n=k)=e^-n n^k/k! (p. 115), is proved by the multinomial count. Normalization, mean and variance are proved.

Durrett Exercise 3.1.2 (p. 115) gets the sqrt(2 pi n) limit with an explicit uniform log remainder. The interval consequence, which the source marks as outside the exercise, is also proved, with exact indices, Chebyshev cutoffs and the endpoint variants.
Durrett's gamma(a) (Exercise 3.1.3) and the rate a-1-a log a = -I(a) (Exercise 3.1.4) are defined, with the 0 log 0 and log 0 conventions.
Durrett Exercise 3.1.3 for a in (0,1) (p. 115) is proved by his hint (point mass with k/n->a, successive ratio, P(S>=k)<=C P(S=k)). The endpoint and outside-range rates are proved separately.
Durrett Exercise 3.1.4 for a>1 (p. 115) is proved by the same hint, with the geometric factor (1-1/a)^-1. The cases a=1, 0<a<1 and a<=0 are proved without the singular factor.

The fixed-p extension is declared as an extension. The uniform local limit (Taylor bound on D(t||p)), the interval and CDF limits, convergence in distribution in the route's sense, and p=0 or 1 degeneracy are all proved.

components.gap: Feller II.9 p. 52 makes a normative judgement about the two error notions: the difference of the two sides of (9.1) grows without bound, but the percentage (relative) error is the one that really matters. The route records the two facts and the distinction: body lines 316-318, annex lines 695-708 ('the source distinction between absolute and percentage error'), and distributions-transforms-and-moment-problems-w02c-p15-011.tex lines 88-92 (Feller 'separates two notions of error'). It does not record Feller's claim that the percentage error is the measure that matters. The companion warning (lines 149-159) argues only the opposite caution, that a small percentage error is not a small absolute error. Record Feller's normative claim, and if the warning is kept, state how it qualifies that claim.
components.note: The body and annex prove the relative and absolute error behaviour, the n=5 values, the two rate values, and the dependence, edge-of-support and p_N=1/N failures (via the portmanteau result earlier on the route). The companion certifies all of Feller's p. 52 and p. 54 figures (1!, 2!, 5!, 10!, 100!, the percentages, 2.0007, 120.01, and the extreme-member ratio) and reconciles the printed digits. Numbers were rechecked by machine. Feller's normative 'percentage error is what matters' claim is missing (see gap).

The route claim is verified. All of Durrett Section 3.1 (Lemma 3.1.1, Theorems 3.1.2-3.1.3, Exercises 3.1.1-3.1.4 and the closing remarks, the remarks via the companion) is supplied. So are Feller's II.9 proof and the VII.2 constant determination. The extension, the weak-convergence support and the next presentations (characteristic functions, CLT) exist on the route.

duties.duty: Both chapter files and the companion record are reached by the recursive input route.
Results the chapter uses without proving them (Gaussian normalization, cosine-integral central coefficient, convergence in distribution, closed-set portmanteau bound) are proved earlier on the route.

The held sources were opened at the cited locators and compared item by item: Durrett printed pp. 113-115 (PDF pp. 121-123), and Feller printed pp. 51-54, 150-151, 174-175 and 179-181 (PDF pp. 66-69, 165-166, 189-190 and 194-196).
